# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

content.text:
I found no blockers. The only findings are small spec edge cases and readability nits.

/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/effects.rs:206: [minor] Vertical mosaic only saves a BG's line when `line % mosaic_height == 0` and that BG uses mosaic on that line. A frame can turn on BGxCNT bit 6, enable the BG, or change MOSAIC V-size partway through a mosaic block. The rest of that block then reads a saved line from an earlier frame, or the initial all-transparent line. gbatek has each block repeat its first line, so this output is wrong. Suggested fix: also save the line when the BG was not using mosaic on the previous line, or save every enabled BG's first block line whether or not it uses mosaic. The existing `ponytail:` comment covers mid-block scroll changes but not this case.
/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/mod.rs:167: [minor] Ownership is borderline. The branch adds a `mosaic_source_lines` field to the shared `Ppu` struct and its initialiser (line 183). The "compositor in `ppu/mod.rs`" entry in PLAN.md arguably covers this, but the sprites and affine workers also edit this struct, so merging may conflict. Suggested fix: the integrator should check for conflicts with the other Phase 3 branches when merging. No other files outside `ppu/effects.rs` and `ppu/mod.rs` are touched.
/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/effects.rs:171: [minor] `compose_line` is about 95 lines: closures, the mosaic setup and a long per-pixel loop. Suggested fix: move the window lookup, the mosaic setup and the per-pixel layer collection into small named helpers.
/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/effects.rs:107: [minor] `alpha_blend` is a dense one-liner (`[0,1,2].map(...)` with indexing, a multiply, a shift and a clamp). `brighten`/`darken` are similar. Suggested fix: add a helper that applies a function to each channel (`map_channels(first, second, |a, b| ...)`), or write out the three channels.
/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/effects.rs:71: [minor] The gbatek field names `eva`, `evb`, `evy` have no plain-English comment where they are defined (the BLDALPHA/BLDY constants describe them, the struct does not). Suggested fix: add `// 1st target weight /16` and similar.
/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/effects.rs:16: [minor] The constants `DISPCNT_WINDOW0_ENABLE`, `DISPCNT_WINDOW1_ENABLE`, `DISPCNT_OBJ_WINDOW_ENABLE` (lines 16-18) and `BGCNT_MOSAIC` (line 19) have no comment, unlike the register constants above them. The names are clear enough. Suggested fix: add a short comment for consistency.

**Checked against gbatek and correct:**
- **Windows:**
  - Window 0 takes precedence over window 1, which beats the OBJ window, which beats outside.
  - Garbage X2>240 or X1>X2 is read as X2=240, and the same for Y with 160.
  - The OBJ window needs both DISPCNT bits 12 and 15.
  - Bit 5 of the window control gates effects.
- **Colour effects:**
  - EVA, EVB and EVY values of 17-31 act as 16.
  - The alpha, brighten and darken formulas match gbatek.
  - Semi-transparent sprites always count as 1st target and always alpha-blend when the pixel below is a 2nd target. Otherwise they fall back to BLDCNT brightness, which matches gbatek's "Semi-Transparent OBJs" section.
  - The backdrop counts as target bit 5.
- **Priority:** OBJ is in front of a BG of equal priority, and BG0 beats BG3 on ties.
- **Mosaic:** Horizontal mosaic repeats the block's first pixel, including its transparency, and windows are applied at the real x.

**Other checks:**
- **Per-ROM hacks:** none.
- **Originality:** the structure (top-two pixel selection, a depth key, a `BlendSettings` struct) is plain and every part traces to gbatek. Nothing is credited to or names another emulator, and there are no unexplained tables.
- **Tests:** four new unit tests cover the blend maths, clamping garbage window values, priority with windows and semi-transparent sprites, and horizontal mosaic. Vertical mosaic has no unit test.
- **Builds:**
  - `cargo test`: 102 passed, no warnings.
  - The wasm release build succeeds.
- **`run_rom`, 120 frames:**
  - `tonc/win-demo` shows the window cut-out correctly.
  - `tonc/bld-demo` and `tonc/mos-demo` render the BG. Their sprite is missing, which is expected because `obj.rs` is not on this branch.
- **Grading:** I did not run the grader, as instructed.
